rubrics.justification: Describes a good-quality expanded/collapsed blastocyst with compact ICM and reasonable TE, which is broadly plausible, but questions the reported 4AA/hatching status and notes features like granularity/early compaction that are not clearly supportable from a single image.

Integrates key factors well: very young age, strong ovarian reserve, male-factor context, good endometrium, prior failed cycle, and adverse lifestyle factors. Could more explicitly weigh BMI and semen parameters against the male-factor label.

Overall logic is consistent and the prognosis follows from embryo quality plus patient factors. Minor issues include somewhat shifting probability ranges and speculative comments about fresh transfer/progesterone without provided data.

Recommendations are largely consistent with IVF practice: favoring SET in a 22-year-old with a high-grade blastocyst, cautioning on smoking/alcohol, and not overusing PGT-A in a very young patient. Small deviations include speculative protocol comments not anchored to available data.

Provides practical next steps for transfer, lifestyle modification, SET, and escalation plans after repeated failure. Useful and case-specific, though some recommendations remain somewhat general rather than tightly protocol-driven.
